plain.li: [opt0] We bought an old adventurer's gear. {X_nameDef} told us where every dent came from, which took a while.
[opt1,safe] {X_nameDef} is staying. Forty years on the road, and {X_pronoun} picked us.
[opt1,risk] Asked {X_nameDef} to stay. {X_nameDef} has a sister to see first. I think {X_pronoun} might come back.
[opt2] Stayed up late listening to {X_nameDef}. Half the stories can't be true. I'd still like to hear them again.
[opt3] An old adventurer came through and the council sent {X_objective} on. I'd have liked to hear a story or two.

warm.li: [opt1,safe] {X_nameDef} unpacked by the window so {X_pronoun} can see the road. Old habit, {X_pronoun} says.

cheerful.li: [opt2] {X_nameDef} once fought a bear with a frying pan, apparently! I'm choosing to believe it.

blunt.li: [opt0] Good gear, fair price. The stories were free.

cold.li: [opt0] Bought forty years of someone's career, by the piece. Sound purchase.

plain.li: [opt0] We paid a mapmaker to walk our hills. {X_nameDef} works with a chain and a compass and doesn't talk much.
[opt1,safe] Up in the hills all day with {X_nameDef}. I know how to read a contour line now, and we know where to dig.
[opt1,risk] A whole day guiding {X_nameDef} over every rock we own. Not one seam worth digging. My feet hurt.
[opt2] A mapmaker offered to survey the land, and folded up the charts and went on. I'd have liked to see how it's done.

cheerful.li: [opt1,safe] {X_nameDef} let me hold the compass for most of the day!

gloomy.li: [opt1,risk] Walked every hill for nothing. The hills don't care what we need.

plain.li: [opt0] A guest who doesn't talk is sitting by the fields. I sat near {X_objective} for a while this afternoon. It helped more than I'd like to admit.
[opt1] The council asked the silent guest to sit with me. We sat all day. I didn't know I needed that.
[opt1] Sat with {X_nameDef} from morning until the light went. Neither of us said a word, and I slept like a stone.
[opt2] A silent traveler asked to sit near us for a day. The council sent {X_objective} on.

warm.li: [opt1] {X_nameDef} touched my shoulder once, when it got dark, and then went to sleep in the grass.

gloomy.li: [opt1] One quiet day doesn't fix anything. It was still the best day I've had in a while.

blunt.li: [opt0] Odd guest. Quiet. I don't mind quiet.

cold.li: [opt2] Sent away a stranger who wanted nothing. Easy decision.

plain.li: [opt0] A limb-maker fitted me with a {TALE} today. I've been trying it out on everything since.
[opt1] The colony paid in materials for my {TALE}. I'm going to earn every bit of it back.
[opt0] It rubs, and I don't care. I have a {TALE}.
[opt2] The limb-maker went on with {X_possessive} cart. I'll manage as I am.

cheerful.li: [opt0] New {TALE}! I keep finding reasons to show it to people.

warm.li: [opt1] Whoever thought to spend our stores on me, thank you.

gloomy.li: [opt2] There was a {TALE} on that cart that would have fit me. I watched it go.

plain.li: [opt0] We put silver into {X_nameDef}'s caravan. I shook on it. If it goes wrong, that's my hand on the deal.
[opt1] We put half in with {X_nameDef}. Half is plenty to lose, if it comes to that.
[opt2] Turned down {X_nameDef}'s venture. Twice the stake in ten days is the kind of promise I don't trust.

cheerful.li: [opt0] We're investors now! I've already spent the profit in my head.

gloomy.li: [opt0] I'll be watching the road for {X_nameDef}'s caravan from tomorrow. It isn't due for ten days.

blunt.li: [opt2] Smelled like a swindle. Said no.

plain.li: [opt0,safe] I found {X_nameDef} bleeding in the brush, and now {X_pronoun} is asleep in one of our beds.
[opt0,risk] We took {X_nameDef} in, and the people who hurt {X_objective} are coming. I'd find {X_objective} again and do the same.
[opt1] I left {X_nameDef} bread and clean bandages where {X_pronoun} could reach them, and came home. I'll go and look tomorrow.
[opt2] I found someone hurt out past the fields and the council said to leave them. I did.

warm.li: [opt0,safe] {X_nameDef} squeezed my hand when we carried {X_objective} in. Didn't say a word.

gloomy.li: [opt2] I keep thinking about the wounded stranger. I walked past. That's all there is to it.

blunt.li: [opt0,risk] They want {X_nameDef}. They'll have to come through us.

cold.li: [opt1] Supplies left, no risk taken. Whether {X_nameDef} lives is up to {X_nameDef}.

plain.li: [opt0] A reeve came for a tithe and we paid. I could have argued, if anyone had asked me to.
[opt1] We paid the lord's tithe in sacks. {X_nameDef} counted every one into the ledger, and the lord's carters will get the good ones, of course.
[opt2,safe] Argued the reeve out of the tithe, boundary stone by boundary stone. I've never been so tired from talking.
[opt2,risk] I argued, and {X_nameDef} had the deed. Now we're paying a fine for my trouble.
[opt3] The reeve got no tithe from us. {X_nameDef} wrote a long line in the ledger and underlined it twice.

cheerful.li: [opt2,safe] Beat a reeve with nothing but my mouth! {X_nameDef} looked like {X_pronoun} had swallowed a lemon.

gloomy.li: [opt2,risk] I lost the argument and it cost us extra. I should have kept quiet.

blunt.li: [opt3] We owe no lord. Said so.

cold.li: [opt0] Paid the tithe. Cheaper than a quarrel with {FACTION}.

plain.li: [opt0,safe] I answered the signal today. Whatever answered back, I'm glad I did.
[opt0,risk] I answered the signal, and it was bait. That's on me.
[opt1,safe] Traced the signal without saying a word into it. It led somewhere on our own land.
[opt1,risk] Lost the signal after hours of chasing it. It just faded, like it had never been there.
[opt2] A signal came in on the comms, and we left it alone. I listened to it loop until it stopped.

cheerful.li: [opt1,safe] Found the source of a mystery signal! It's the best afternoon of work I've had.

gloomy.li: [opt0,risk] I keep hearing that laughter on the channel. I gave us away.

blunt.li: [opt2] Signal ignored. Probably for the best.

cold.li: [opt1,safe] Triangulated an unknown transmitter. Recovered the contents. Efficient.

plain.li: [opt0] Lightning split the old {BEAST}, and the council let me have the heartwood. I've already got an idea for it.
[opt1] The lightning-struck {BEAST} was cut for timber. Good wood. I'd have done something better with it.
[opt2] We left the lightning tree standing. I walk past it every morning now.

cheerful.li: [opt0] I've never worked wood like this! It's hard as stone and dark all the way through.

warm.li: [opt2] The lightning tree is ours now. Someone has already tied a ribbon on it.

plain.li: [opt0,safe] Smoked out the wild bees and got the comb. Only two stings, and I'm not counting the one on my ear.
[opt0,risk] The bees won. I ran. I'm told I ran very fast.
[opt1] We left the wild bees alone. They're busy in the fields from dawn to dusk.

cheerful.li: [opt0,safe] Honeycomb for supper, and I'm the one who got it!

gloomy.li: [opt0,risk] Chased halfway home by bees. I'll be hearing about it for a year.

blunt.li: [opt1] Left the bees. They earn their keep.

plain.li: [opt0,safe] I made a {TALE} from a fallen star. I've picked it up a dozen times tonight just to hold it.
[opt0,risk] The star-iron cracked in the quench. All that work, and it's ordinary steel now.
[opt1] We broke up the fallen star for its metal. Good steel. Still, it fell out of the sky.
[opt2] We left the fallen star where it landed. I go out and look at it in the evenings.

cheerful.li: [opt0,safe] Forged from a fallen star, and I did it! Well, it's the colony's, but still.

gloomy.li: [opt0,risk] It cracked. Of course it cracked.

blunt.li: [opt0,safe] Forged star-iron. Best work I've done.

cold.li: [opt1] Meteoric iron, reduced to stock. Practical.

plain.li: [opt0,safe] The {BEAST} at the gate led me into the hills, and it knew where it was going. I came home with something to show for it.
[opt0,risk] Followed the {BEAST} all morning and lost it in a thicket. Maybe I wasn't meant to see where it went.
[opt1] We left the {BEAST} an offering, and in the evening it was gone, and so was the food.
[opt2] The council marked the {BEAST} for the hunters. I didn't like it.
[opt3] The {BEAST} stood at the gate half the day and then walked away. I wish I knew what it wanted.

warm.li: [opt1] Leaving the offering felt right. My grandmother would have done the same.

gloomy.li: [opt2] We're hunting the sign. Nothing good comes of that.

plain.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} knew me from the old days. The colony paid to keep it quiet. I owe them for that.
[opt1,safe] {X_nameDef} said a name I haven't used in years, got no silver for it, and left. I didn't sleep.
[opt1,risk] {X_nameDef} told {FACTION} what I was. I used to be {TALE}. I'm not any more, but that's not what they'll hear.
[opt2,safe] I took {X_nameDef} for a walk and we talked. {X_nameDef} won't be bothering anyone.
[opt2,risk] I tried talking to {X_nameDef}. It went badly, and now {FACTION} will know.

gloomy.li: [opt1,risk] By the end of the week they'll all know what I was. I'd nearly forgotten it myself.

warm.li: [opt0] The council paid for my past without asking me a single question about it.

plain.li: [opt0] A letter from {X_nameDef}, my old commander. {X_nameDef} is fighting {ENEMY} now, and we sent what we could.
[opt0] We sent supplies to {X_nameDef}'s campaign. I wrote a note to go with them and tore up three versions first.
[opt1] {X_nameDef} asked for help against {ENEMY}, and all we sent was good wishes.

warm.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} still signs letters the way {X_pronoun} did in the old days. I'd know that hand anywhere.

gloomy.li: [opt1] My old commander asked me for help, and I sent a letter. I'll have to live with that.

blunt.li: [opt0] Old unit needed supplies. Sent them.

plain.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} came all this way to thank me for something I'd forgotten I did. I remember now. It was a long night.
[opt1,safe] {X_nameDef}, who I patched up years ago, is staying with us. I'll have to make sure {X_pronoun} doesn't need patching again.
[opt1,risk] Asked {X_nameDef} to stay. There's family waiting for {X_objective}. Good. That's what I kept {X_objective} alive for.
[opt2] {X_nameDef} is going to tell the whole road about me. I'm not sure how I feel about that.

warm.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} still has the scar where I stitched {X_objective}. Neat work, if I say so myself.

cheerful.li: [opt2] Apparently I'm famous now, at least on one road.

blunt.li: [opt0] Old patient. Brought a gift. Kind of {X_objective}.

plain.li: [opt0] Found an old map from back when I was {TALE}. The council wants to follow it up. So do I.
[opt1] Found an old map in my things from my life before. I've put it away. I take it out at night sometimes.

cheerful.li: [opt0] An old map and a cross on it! I feel like a child again.

gloomy.li: [opt1] Folded the map back along its old creases. There are places on it I don't want to see again.

cold.li: [opt0] Located an old cache. Worth retrieving.

plain.li: [opt0] I found something and we looked at it all evening. I drew it from four sides. I'm going to find another one.
[opt1] I found a treasure and I get to keep it. It's on my shelf.
[opt2] I found something and they sold it. It was the best thing I ever found.

cheerful.li: [opt0] I asked a hundred questions and got a hundred answers!

gloomy.li: [opt2] I'm not going to show them the next thing I find.

warm.li: [opt1] I check on my treasure every morning. It's still there.
